title: faceto — event-sourced (the log is truth; the model is a projection replayed from it)

elements.label: on a successful command, append its event
on read: skip unknown kinds (fwd compat), upcast a renamed kind (bwd compat)
a frontier move re-borders its neighbour — the partition stays gap-free (normalize)
on append, re-project on next read (cache keyed on log hash)
lint the model on read; suppress a finding once its element is resolved
client polls /model-version; on change, swap the SVG
when the log grows past threshold, compact
Who mints ids for added elements & regions?
elements.detail: Ids are minted server-side, never by the client: <PREFIX><N>, one past the highest suffix ever added under that lane's prefix in the log (removed-but-not-compacted ids stay reserved), computed under the appends lock so concurrent adds can't collide. Regions share the rule via resolve_region_id (K<n>).
elements.resolution: Server-side, monotonic per prefix. mint_id in serve.rs and resolve_region_id in the replay both take 'one past the highest ever seen'; a freed suffix is never reused.

elements.label: Event schema versioning / migration over time
elements.detail: Schema grows by additive change (new optional fields ignored, new event kinds skipped on read = forward compat); a renamed event *kind* is migrated forward at events::upcast, the single read-path seam (backward compat), shape-detected so no version counter and no log-format change. Fields evolve additively only. Seeded with CommentAdded/Comment → ElementAnnotated.
elements.resolution: Additive-first + an upcast seam. Unknown kinds/fields tolerated on read; a renamed kind is repaired in one place before parse_event; semantics never change in place.

elements.label: Concurrency: ordering of appends from multiple clients
elements.detail: All appends serialize through one mutex in serve.rs so concurrent POST /comment handlers never interleave a half-written line and the log's order is causal.
elements.resolution: One appends mutex. Every write path (structural op or annotation) takes it, so file order = causal order and mint_id reads a consistent watermark.

elements.label: Replay cost: rebuild per request, or cache the projection?
elements.detail: Cache the projection: version = fnv12(log bytes); reuse serve.rs's existing ring keyed on the log hash; replay only on a cache miss; compact caps replay length by folding to a snapshot.
elements.resolution: Cache, keyed on the log's content hash. Replay runs only when a new event lands; compact bounds the tail.

elements.label: Is model.json a derived snapshot, or gone entirely?
elements.detail: log-only (pure ES): model.json is derived & gitignored, never hand-edited; the log is the only write path; render & serve replay the log; an existing model.json bootstraps as a genesis batch of events. F-auto-genesis killed the legacy serve-from-model mode entirely.
elements.resolution: Derived, not truth. event-log.jsonl is the only durable record and only write path; model.json is disposable bootstrap output.

elements.label: Migrate the legacy comments.jsonl inbox into the log
elements.detail: faceto genesis folds a sibling comments.jsonl after the model's genesis batch: each stored comment maps through events::comment_to_events (the same mapping the live server uses) into ElementAnnotated/HotspotResolved/ElementRenamed/ElementMoved/ElementRemoved. Best-effort: blank/unparseable/elemId-less lines are skipped and counted.
elements.resolution: Fold into genesis. comment_to_events is the single source of truth, shared with POST /comment; the legacy inbox lands on the board instead of being stranded.

elements.label: Can regions overlap or leave holes?
elements.detail: No. Regions are a contiguous partition of the timeline. Frontier moves set one border and replay's normalize re-borders the neighbour atomically; legacy independent spans (PhaseResized) are projected onto a gap-free, overlap-free partition too. Remove = merge under the partition (the neighbour absorbs the freed columns; a board-end removal extends the outermost survivor).
elements.resolution: Never. model::normalize projects any phase history onto a contiguous partition, shared by replay and from_json so every Model is a partition whatever its source.
